label: late copy-phase outputs (recalling original position 5+)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase. It never fires on original-phase inputs or on the <DEL> step. Almost all activation mass (96%) is on steps that output original token 5 or later (recall_idx 5-6 carry 81% of mass), so it is mostly the last one to three outputs of long sequences (L=6-9). The rate is highest when to_go = 0, and higher for L=7-8 than for L=9. Steps with recall_idx 2-4 in short sequences (L=3-5) fire only weakly and rarely. It is sparse inside that window, though: only about 36% of qualifying steps fire, and I found no simple condition that decides which ones. Some output tokens fire more often (v, n, w, a, q: rate 0.16-0.23 vs about 0.12 overall), but restricting to them costs a lot of recall. Input-token identity, first token, digit count and repeats have little effect. The largest activations sit on the second-to-last or last output of L=6-7 sequences.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the next token to output (most: v, w, -, n, a, q; least: p, 3, h, r) and the token being output (most: v, n, w, a, q, l; least: 3, r, p, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=5, to_go=0, recall_idx=6.
